title: WIN-014: re-anchor spring-floor derivation to Wang 2000's own residual band (close c14 H1)
scope: Replace the unsourced '1–2 µGal post-fit residual floor' premise (and the network-stacked 0.4–0.7 µGal floor / 4–25× ratio that derives from it) with the Wang et al. 2000 ±3–4 µGal single-instrument residual band — the dome's own cited 1997 Mohe primary source for exactly this LaCoste-Romberg D-series spring class — and the √8-stacked result that follows (~1.1–1.4 µGal network floor, 2× to 8× below the 3–9 µGal κ prediction). Three find/replace patches against data/wins.json plus one alignment patch against test.js's regression anchor.
hole_addressed: WIN-014 c14 H1 (moderate): The load-bearing instrument figure 'post-fit residual floors of approximately 1–2 µGal' for the 2009 seven LaCoste-Romberg springs is uncited, and the EXP-618 paragraph itself quotes the SAME instrument class at ±3–4 µGal residual band from Wang et al. 2000 — visible tension a defender can quote our own paragraph back at us. The derived stacked-floor 0.4–0.7 µGal and 4–25× multiplier inherit the uncited premise.
analyst_assessment: Curmudgeon c14's recommended re-anchoring is sound and arithmetic checks: Wang et al. 2000's stated single-instrument residual band (±3–4 µGal, verified verbatim from arXiv:1003.4947 by EXP-618's primary-source fetch) suppressed by √8 ≈ 2.828 across the network's eight gravimeters yields 1.06–1.41 µGal — i.e., '~1.1–1.4 µGal stacked' — and the predicted-vs-floor ratio is 3/1.41 = 2.12 → 9/1.06 = 8.49, i.e., 2× to 8× below the prediction. Switching premise costs the prose nothing structurally (the dilemma is unchanged: the network either bounded 3–9 µGal and reported zero, or could not bound the signal and the dome's 'CONFIRMED' label loses its empirical handhold) and removes the one number-stack in WIN-014 that didn't come from a cited source. The new derivation comes from exactly the paper EXP-618 already leans on for the symmetric self-defeat — so the entire spring-floor chain now anchors to the dome's own cited 1997 instrument paper. This is the curmudgeon's c14 preemptive recommendation realized.
kernel_of_truth: The defense's instrument-class observation (springs are noisier than SGs) is correct — and after this patch, our derivation acknowledges that observation by adopting Wang 2000's full single-instrument band rather than a smaller, unsourced figure. The 2× to 8× ratio (vs the prior 4× to 25× ratio derived from the smaller, unsourced floor) is the honest figure that flows from the defender's own numbers. The conclusion does not weaken: a 2.1× safety margin between predicted signal and post-stack floor is sufficient to bind a network-wide null at the conservative end of the κ prediction, and 8.5× at the upper end overwhelms it. The price of using the defender's own worst case is a smaller-margin claim — and the margin still wins.

anticipated_objections: Objection: the new '2× to 8×' margin is narrower than the prior '4–1 to 25×' — a defender will say a 2.1× safety factor on the conservative end is fragile. Response: the new number is the defender's own paper's worst-case band, and 2.1× above the predicted lower edge is still well above any rational detection threshold; the defender cannot simultaneously demand we use a smaller floor (to inflate margin) and reject our floor-derivation method (which uses the defender's own number). The honest figure is the bigger story: the network's stated noise floor sits below the prediction even on the defender's worst-case stated band.

Objection: stacking 8 independent residuals by √n assumes uncorrelated noise across sites — atmospheric loading common-mode would degrade that. Response: c14 H3 flags exactly this nit and the curmudgeon-recommended hedge ('under standard uncorrelated-noise assumptions') applies but is not opened as a separate ISS. The 2× lower-edge ratio survives a 50% degradation in stacking efficiency (1.06 × √2 ≈ 1.50 µGal still leaves 3/1.50 = 2× margin at the conservative end). The conclusion is robust to the assumption.

Objection: changing '4–25×' to '2× to 8×' weakens our quantitative claim and the dome will quote our former higher number against us. Response: the dome cannot quote a number we have visibly removed; the c14 review record makes the swap explicit and credible — it is exactly the kind of methodological tightening a critical review is expected to do when a defender's own source quantifies a parameter our prose left unsourced. The narrower margin sourced from the defender's literature is more durable than a wider margin from an unsourced premise.
